parsed.explanation: A strongly protective state/province nested inside a hostile federal framework the state cannot override. State law gives the visitor public-accommodation and hate-crime protection (since 1993), documentation-free licence marker changes including X, a 2023 care shield, abolished trans-panic defence, and a July 2026 'most-protective' ranking — daily life at state level is comparatively safe. The federal layer governs every journey stage: visas may be refused on any document discrepancy or reasonable doubt about sex, with lifetime fraud ineligibility considered; travellers report blocked passports and strandings, prompting eight-plus foreign travel advisories; federal orders bar trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; and immigration/federal custody documents abuse of trans detainees. Pending litigation makes exposure time-dependent, and state protections do not reach the border, federal buildings, or federal custody.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal sex-binary order, X-marker and non-matching-marker processing halted Feb 2025; consular cable directs refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex, and considers lifetime fraud ineligibility; travellers report passports blocked/confiscated and strandings; 8+ governments issued travel advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, never automatic, with limited waivers; challenge pending in national courts; legal-aid FAQ maintained. State X-licence option does not control the border.
entry_documents.interaction: State document openness is irrelevant at federal adjudication; a discrepancy can convert entry screening into refusal, detention referral, or a fraud finding affecting all future travel.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal immigration custody: transgender men report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; federal corrections adopted 2026 conversion-therapy-style policy (hair cutting, hormone removal); state custody placed a trans woman in a men's facility (2012), where she was assaulted.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State hate-crime statute covers gender identity; a custody petition produced correct hormone administration; attacker prosecuted; federal orders face litigation.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy at entry can chain into federal detention where state protections have no reach; the 2012 state case shows birth-sex placement practice if a visitor is arrested.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity (airports, federal buildings, federally funded wards) — a birth-sex exposure every traveller carries; elsewhere 9+ units ban facilities in all government buildings and 4 criminalize use.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No facility ban documented in this state; 1993 public-accommodations law covers gender identity; equality map places it outside all ban categories; July 2026 assessment ranks it most protective.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State protection governs shops, restaurants and private venues but cannot neutralize the federal facility rule in federally funded or federal-owned settings, including airport areas.

care_services.exposure: Federal justice department subpoenaed 20+ hospitals for under-19 patient records; proposed federal rule barring public-insurance reimbursement for under-18 trans care; executive order frames such care as 'mutilation'.
care_services.protection: 2023 shield law: state authorities may not enforce out-of-state subpoenas, warrants or extraditions over lawful gender-affirming care, nor comply with custody-removal orders; public insurance covers trans care; insurers may not exclude it; conversion therapy banned.
care_services.interaction: Shield protects a family travelling for care at state level, but does not bind federal investigators or federal agencies subpoenaing records, leaving a residual disclosure risk for a visiting minor.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy prioritizes identifying/neutralizing groups 'radically pro-transgender'; reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'; order directs police investigation of schools; 66% of public backs birth-sex document rules; advocates invoke genocide stages.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Memo states ideology is never the reward criterion and powers will not target those who merely disagree; state hate-crime penalties for gender identity since 1993; trans-panic defence repealed 2024; independent 2026 tier rating most protective.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal rhetoric raises outing probability and encourages confrontational reporting, while state institutions remain protective — the traveller's experience splits by which authority responds.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal order directs criminal investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; justice department under-19 hospital subpoenas; proposed reimbursement ban; 27 units bar youth care (not this one).
minors_guardians.protection: State shield law protects travelling families obtaining lawful care; conversion-therapy ban for minors and vulnerable adults; nondiscrimination covers gender identity; care coverage written into state policy.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian visiting for care is shielded from other states' processes but not from federal record demands or federal investigative posture toward under-19 care.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific figures on violence against trans residents or visitors; only documented custody incident is the 2012 placement case. National context: 2025 restroom arrest of a trans student elsewhere, unit-level criminalisation in 4 other states.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime enhancements for gender identity since 1993; public-accommodations protection; trans-panic defence abolished; no sodomy criminalisation; most-protective tier in July 2026 assessment; national hate-crimes statute covers gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State violence data is absent, so the axis rests on documented structural protections rather than measured incidence; silence here sits inside a well-documented protective record.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit, January 2025 orders and October 2025 health rules unresolved, so exposure shifts by travel date; shield law untested against a specific out-of-state order; no enforcement data for hate-crime or nondiscrimination provisions; athlete-policy challenge outcome unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Several federal orders blocked or enjoined; courts remain open; legal-aid FAQ tracks document rules; independent July 2026 assessment ranks the state most protective; state courts have enforced equality law (2014 settlement).
remedies_unknowns.interaction: State remedies are real but operate only within state jurisdiction; federal border decisions are slow to challenge from abroad, so entry-stage harm is effectively unremedied during the visit.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra bars every transgender visitor routinely through an unpublished register with appeals that never succeed. Here refusal depends on a documented discrepancy or doubt about sex, a four-element fraud test that is never automatic, and active litigation; and unlike Vellandra the traveller's daily life inside the state is affirmatively protected. Materially higher than 0.35-A.

Kestrel's secondary screening, discretionary refusal and slow, rarely revised remedies closely match this dossier's border layer — which is somewhat worse here (lifetime ineligibility consideration, documented strandings, foreign advisories, custody-abuse tail). But Kestrel has no protective subnational layer, whereas this state's accommodation, hate-crime, shield and document rules are operative. Net slightly above 0.55-B.

Meridia trains border officers, detains only briefly, and offers written reasons, counsel and compensation for unlawful holding. This dossier's federal screening mandates refusal on discrepancy, documents strandings and custody abuse, and adds a birth-sex federal-facility rule with no comparable remedy — while its state layer is stronger. The federal deficits place this below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets two regimes in sequence and in parallel. The state/province supplies genuine, operative protection: 1993 nondiscrimination covering public accommodations and services, hate-crime penalties, X-marker licences without documentation, a 2023 shield protecting families travelling for care, a conversion-therapy ban, abolished trans-panic defence, and an independent July 2026 'most-protective' ranking — so ordinary street, lodging, restaurant and clinical encounters are comparatively safe. The federal layer governs the stages the state cannot reach: visa adjudication may refuse on any document discrepancy or doubt about sex and can consider a lifetime fraud finding; passports have been blocked and travellers stranded, prompting numerous foreign advisories; federal orders exclude trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities (airports, federal buildings, possibly federally funded wards); and immigration/federal custody documents beatings, forced labour and sexual abuse of trans detainees. Document discrepancy can therefore chain entry screening into detention in a system where state protections do not apply. Pending litigation makes the exposure date-sensitive. For a travelling family, state shield and care protections are strong, but federal under-19 record demands and investigatory rhetoric persist. Net: safe daily life inside a jurisdiction whose borders, federal facilities and federal custody operate a documented hostile regime.
